thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Futures Point To Slight Gains, Apple Rally Set To Boost Tech

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Futures Point To Slight Gains, Apple Rally Set To Boost Tech
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Upcoming Fed statement is highly anticipated, though few changes are expected
U.S. stock-index futures were mostly flat on Wednesday, although a blowout quarter at Apple helped to lift technology stocks in premarket trading, which in turn supported Nasdaq-100 futures.
Both the Dow and the S&P 500 futures indicated muted moves, however, as traders braced for a Federal Reserve policy statement, as well as ADP's monthly report on private-sector employment.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Nasdaq-100 futures rose by 13 points, or 0.2%, to 6,704.75, trimming sharper gains.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded roughly flat at 24,075, while S&P 500 futures slipped 1.25 points, or less than 0.1%, to 2,651,75, giving up earlier gains.
On Tuesday, the Dow finished 0.3% lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-street-stocks-ready-to-slip-further-with-pfizer-earnings-ahead-2018-05-01), while the S&P 500 advanced by 0.3% and the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite rose 0.9%.
The Dow and S&P are down 2.5% and 0.7% for the year, as of Tuesday's close. The Nasdaq Composite has climbed 3.3%.
What's driving markets?
Apple's stock (AAPL)rose 3.4% in premarket action after the largest U.S. company by market capitalization late Tuesday posted better-than-anticipated earnings and revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-stock-rises-after-iphone-sales-fall-short-but-earnings-beat-2018-05-01) for the first quarter. As the largest stock in the economy, based on market capitalization, the move should provide an outsize lift to Wall Street overall.
Check out:Apple earnings were saved by the company's new MVP (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-were-saved-by-the-companys-new-mvp-2018-05-01)
And see: The surprise in Apple earnings--big growth in China (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-surprise-in-apple-earnings-big-growth-in-china-2018-05-01)
The iPhone maker was merely the latest high-profile company to top analyst forecasts in its results. However, even better-than-expected earnings haven't been enough to lift the main equity benchmarks out of a tight range in recent weeks, as investors are also worried about protectionism and other geopolitical flare-ups.
Which economic releases are on tap?
Fed officials are due to wrap up a two-day meeting, and the policy makers are expected to leave interest rates on hold (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/as-market-churns-fed-will-say-it-has-inflation-situation-under-control-2018-04-26). Market participants are watching for any change to plans for a tightening path of two more rate increases in 2018. Changes to Fed policy--including both higher rates and a shrinking balance sheet--are seen as one of the primary risks to stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/forget-trade-heres-the-real-risk-to-the-stock-market-2018-04-05) over the remainder of the year.
The Federal Open Market Committee's policy statement is slated to hit at 2 p.m. Eastern Time.
Don't miss: Why the Fed could make 4 rate hikes this year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-will-make-4-rate-hikes-this-year-economists-say-after-latest-gdp-eci-reports-2018-04-27)
In the latest economic data, the private sector added 204,000 jobs in April (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-204000-private-sector-jobs-in-april-adp-2018-05-02), according to ADP, down from the 241,000 added in the previous month.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
What are market analysts saying?
"Market expectations for this Fed meeting are straightforward. No rate hike on Wednesday, but a more hawkish communiqué," said Nicholas Colas, co-founder of DataTrek Research.
"What matters more to markets is this question: 'Where will fed funds be at the end of 2019?' Will we have to relive the '3 vs. 4 rate increases' debate next year as well? This hasn't been a friendly narrative for U.S. stocks this year, although high valuations and twitchy long-term rates haven't helped either.
Which stocks are in focus?
In addition to Apple, quarterly earnings remain a primary focus for investors.
Snap Inc.(SNAP) plummeted 20% a day after reporting revenue and active daily users that were below forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/snap-redesign-flops-sending-stock-down-19-as-analysts-slash-targets-2018-05-02).
Yum Brands Inc. (YUM) reported first-quarter earnings and sales that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/yum-brands-tops-earnings-estimates-backs-2018-guidance-2018-05-02). The fast-food chain operator also affirmed its full-year guidance.
CVS Health Corp.(CVS) reported adjusted first-quarter earnings that beat expectations, along with better-than-expected sales (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cvs-shares-rise-after-profit-beats-views-2018-05-02).
Southern Co.(SO) reported first-quarter revenue that beat expectations, and earnings that were helped by the recently passed tax bill (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/southern-co-profit-boosted-by-tax-revamp-2018-05-02).
Madison Square Garden Co. (MSG) swung to a first-quarter profit and reported revenue that topped analyst forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/madison-square-garden-surprises-with-profit-and-revenue-beat-2018-05-02).
Wyndham Worldwide Corp.(WYN) reported a sharp drop in its first-quarter earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wyndham-worldwide-profit-falls-62-2018-05-02), although sales rose modestly.
SodaStream International Ltd.(SODA) reported first-quarter earnings that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sodastream-shares-jump-after-earnings-beat-and-guidance-raised-2018-05-02). It also raised its outlook.
After the market closes, earnings releases should come from Kraft Heinz Co. (KHC) and Tesla Inc. (TSLA), among others.
Esperion Therapeutics Inc.(ESPR) announced results for a late-stage clinical trial (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/esperion-shares-halted-on-positive-late-stage-trial-results-2018-05-02) of its cholesterol-lowering medication. The stock fell 20% in premarket trading after having previously been halted.
What are other markets doing?
European stocks rose modestly, supported by upbeat corporate results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-as-upbeat-corporate-updates-roll-in-2018-05-02). U.K. stocks added 0.4%.
Markets in Asia were little changed. Stocks in Japan dipped 0.2%. Investors were awaiting cues from U.S.-China trade negotiations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-quiet-awaiting-upcoming-economic-data-2018-05-01), along with the release of both a raft of April manufacturing data from Asia and the Federal Reserve's latest policy statement.
Gold futures rose 0.3%, while oil futures rose 0.3%. The ICE U.S. Dollar Index fell less than 0.1% a day after turning positive for 2018.
